pool.question: Camp's underway. What's the one thing you're locking in before Week 1?

options.text: Making sure everybody in this locker room trusts each other before it counts.
My conditioning. I want to be the freshest guy on the field in the fourth quarter all year.
Chemistry with the guys around me. Stats can wait.
My routine. Same process every single day, no shortcuts.

pool.question: How do you want this team talked about once the season actually starts?

options.text: As a team nobody wants to see in a big spot.
As a team that plays for each other, every snap.
As the most entertaining team in the league to watch.
As a team people remember for a long time.

pool.question: What's been the biggest challenge for you in camp so far?

options.text: Nothing's a real challenge yet. It's still just practice to me.
Making sure the young guys are picking things up as fast as I am.
Honestly? Staying patient. I want the season to already be here.
Finding new ways to stand out before the cameras show up for real games.

pool.question: Every camp has a battle for playing time. How are you approaching yours?

options.text: However it shakes out, I'll be the best teammate to whoever wins the job.
I don't lose competitions. Simple as that.
I let the coaches sort it out. I just show up and work.
I want my name in that conversation for years to come, not just this camp.

pool.question: What's one thing you worked on this offseason that people don't know about?

options.text: Film. I probably watched more tape than anyone in this building.
A part of my game I know people are going to be surprised by.
Just being a better teammate, honestly. That's a skill too.
Handling pressure. I wanted this to be the year nothing rattles me.

pool.question: The pads are on now. How different does this camp feel from a year ago?

options.text: Feels like a team that actually expects to win now.
Feels closer. Like a real family in this building.
Feels the same to me. I show up the same way regardless.
Feels like the start of something people are going to talk about.

pool.question: What's your honest read on this roster heading into the season?

options.text: We're deeper than people think. That's going to matter in December.
We're talented enough to make some noise. I'll leave it there.
We've got dogs in this building. Ask anybody who's been at practice.
We've got guys who are going to make this fun to watch.

pool.question: If you had to set one personal goal for this season right now, what is it?

options.text: Winning. Nothing else on my list matters if we don't win.
Being the same guy in Week 1 that I am in Week 18.
Making everyone around me better than they were last year.
Putting up a season people still bring up years from now.

pool.question: How do you handle the grind of camp without losing your edge?

options.text: I remind myself every rep counts toward something bigger.
I stay even. Good day or bad day, same guy tomorrow.
I compete in literally everything, even the drills nobody's watching.
I lean on the guys next to me. Nobody grinds through camp alone.

pool.question: What's the vibe like in the building right now, before a single game's been played?

options.text: Loud. Confident. Maybe a little too confident, but I like it.
Focused. Everybody knows what's actually at stake this year.
Calm. We've been here before. No need to overreact to camp hype.
Hungry. I don't think this group is satisfied with almost.

pool.question: The front office has been busy. How are you feeling about the moves so far?

options.text: I trust the front office. They've earned that.
I'm excited. Feels like this team is building toward something real.
Whoever's in this locker room, I'll make it work. I always have.
Bring in whoever you want. I'm still the standard in this building.

pool.question: New faces are showing up around the building. What's your message to them?

options.text: My door's open. Whatever you need to get comfortable, come find me.
Earn it. Nobody's handed anything here, myself included.
Welcome to the family. We take care of our own.
Get your camera ready, because we're about to make some noise together.

pool.question: This is a business, and rosters turn over. How do you deal with watching teammates leave?

options.text: It's hard. Those relationships don't just end because the jersey changes.
I stay professional about it. That's the job.
I use it as motivation. Nobody's spot is guaranteed, including mine.
I make sure their legacy in this building isn't forgotten.

pool.question: Your own name's going to come up in these conversations eventually. Does that cross your mind?

options.text: I don't think about it. I just try to be a guy this team wants to keep.
I want to be here. I want my whole story written in this building.
That's a conversation for another day. Right now I'm just trying to win.
Let them try to replace me. I'll make that decision look bad.

pool.question: What do you make of the new additions to the roster?

options.text: Talented. I've already been in the building with a couple of them.
It raises the bar. Good. I want that.
More weapons means more ways to win together. I love it.
It's going to make this the most fun team to watch in the league.

pool.question: How closely are you following the moves other teams around the league are making?

options.text: Closely enough to know exactly who we have to be ready for.
Not really my job. I worry about what happens in this building.
Every move somebody else makes is one more reason to outwork them.
Enough to know we're going to have some fun rivalries this year.

pool.question: Roster turnover changes a locker room's identity. What do you want this team's identity to be?

options.text: Physical. Relentless. A team nobody enjoys playing.
Together. Whatever we accomplish, we accomplish as one group.
Disciplined. We're not beating ourselves this year.
Memorable. I want people telling stories about this roster for years.

pool.question: What's your take on how the team is building around you specifically?

options.text: I don't need it built around me. I make whoever's next to me better.
I see it. And I appreciate it. I plan to make good on it.
That's their job. Mine is to be undeniable regardless.
I try not to think about that stuff. I just show up and play.

pool.question: There's a lot of roster movement across the league right now. Does any of it get your attention?

options.text: A little. Keeps you sharp knowing the landscape's shifting.
Some of it, sure. Makes for good storylines this year.
Not really. My focus stays in this building.
Only in the sense that it tells me who I need to go prove something against.

pool.question: If you could describe this offseason's roster building in one word, what would it be?

options.text: "Intentional." Nothing about this felt random.
"Hungry." Everybody added feels like they've got something to prove.
"Family." This still feels like our locker room, just bigger.
"Historic." I think people look back on this offseason differently one day.

pool.question: There's a new voice in the building now that coaching's changed hands. First impression?

options.text: Direct. No wasted words. I respect that.
Demanding. Which is exactly what this team needed.
Genuine. It's clear they actually care about this locker room as people.
Confident. They walked in like they belong here, and I respect that too.

pool.question: New staff usually means a new system. How's the adjustment going?

options.text: It's a process, but I trust it. I'll get there.
I picked it up fast. That's kind of what I do.
I've made sure I'm not the only one figuring it out. We're learning it together.
I'm treating it like a chance to reintroduce myself to this league.

pool.question: What do you think this new coaching staff needs to see from you specifically?

options.text: That I'm somebody they can build the whole operation around.
Consistency. Same guy on tape every single week.
That I'll do whatever role they ask, no ego about it.
That I show up in big moments. That's never been a question for me.

pool.question: A coaching change shakes a lot of players up. How did you take the news?

options.text: I stayed even. Change is part of this business.
I saw it as an opportunity, honestly. New voice, clean slate.
I made sure the locker room knew we control what we can control.
It fired me up. New staff means everybody's earning their spot again.

pool.question: What are you hoping stays the same under the new staff, no matter what else changes?

options.text: This locker room's culture. That's ours, not the coaching staff's.
The standard. I don't care who's calling plays, the bar doesn't move.
The identity we've built. That took real work to earn.
Honestly, I'm open to all of it changing. I adapt fine.

pool.question: How would you sum up the new coaching staff's approach so far?

options.text: Detail-obsessed. Nothing gets past them in these meetings.
High-energy. Practice actually feels different now.
Player-first. They actually listen to what we're seeing on the field.
No-nonsense. Exactly what a locker room like this needed.

pool.question: Now that the season's officially in the books, what's your honest read on how it went?

options.text: There's real stuff to build on. I saw it, even if the record doesn't show it.
Not good enough. I don't sugarcoat that.
This locker room grew closer through it, and that matters to me.
It's a chapter. I'm already thinking about the next one.

pool.question: Some teammates are moving on now that the season's over. Anything you want to say to them?

options.text: Thank you. Genuinely. This locker room doesn't work without them.
I'll remember what we built together, wherever they end up.
Go be great. I mean that.
It's part of the deal. I stay focused on what's next for me.

pool.question: Looking back, what's the moment from this season that sticks with you most?

options.text: Honestly, the quiet moments in the locker room, not the highlights.
The moment I knew I could take over a game whenever I needed to.
A moment I think people are going to remember for a long time.
Honestly, none of it rattled me enough to stick out. That's the point.

pool.question: What's the biggest lesson you're taking out of this season?

options.text: That leadership is about showing up the same way every single day.
That we're only as good as how we play for each other.
That I still have another level, and I plan on finding it.
That staying even, win or lose, is the only way to last in this game.

pool.question: With players leaving the program, how do you think about your own future here?

options.text: I'm not going anywhere. I want to help build whatever comes next.
I focus on what I can control. The rest sorts itself out.
Whatever happens, I want this locker room to know I had their back.
I want to be the guy this program is still talking about years from now.

pool.question: The offseason grind is underway. What does a normal day look like for you right now?

options.text: Film, weight room, recovery. Same three things, every day.
Whatever it takes to make sure I'm the best version of myself by kickoff.
A lot of it is staying connected with teammates, even away from the building.
Building the version of myself people are going to be talking about next year.

pool.question: What's the mood around the program during this stretch of the offseason?

options.text: Optimistic. There's real belief in what we're building.
Businesslike. Everybody knows the work isn't done.
Tight-knit. This group genuinely likes being around each other.
Confident, maybe a little loud about it. I like that energy.

pool.question: What are you personally most excited about heading into next season?

options.text: Proving what this team is actually capable of.
Watching this group take the next step together.
Adding another chapter to what I'm building here.
Honestly, just getting back to playing meaningful football again.

pool.question: How are you staying sharp during a stretch with no games on the schedule?

options.text: I treat every offseason rep like it's a real game rep.
Routine. It's boring, but it works.
Pushing the guys around me to stay sharp too. It's a group effort.
Thinking about the legacy I want to leave and working backward from there.
